text:
For a lot of cells at once, I'd go with a 16-bay charger with independent slots. The sources are affiliate review sites, and I couldn't verify prices or direct purchase links for most of these, so treat this as a shortlist.

## Top pick for bulk charging: Tenergy TN438 (16 bays)
- It charges AA and AAA NiMH/NiCd in any combination, and an LCD shows the status of each cell.
- It has protection against overcharge, overheating, short-circuit and reverse polarity, plus an 8-hour timer. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/))
- I didn't get a price or a buy link for it. Search the name on Tenergy's store or Amazon.

## Other 16-bay options
- **BONAI 16-Bay:** It takes mixed AA/AAA in any slot, runs on 110-240V AC at 250-500mA per port, and has per-port LEDs. It can't charge alkaline or lithium cells. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-aaa-charger/))
- **POWEROWL 16-Bay:** It has 16 independent channels and a four-stage charge (pre-charge, quick, floating, trickle). ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-battery-chargers/))
- **CITYORK 16-Bay:** It has a smart LCD and a ventilated design for heat. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/))

## If 8 bays is enough: Tenergy TN480U, $23.99
- Each slot has its own LCD readout. It charges AA at 500mA and AAA at 250mA, and it ends the charge by negative delta-V with bad-cell detection.
- It runs from any USB-C 5V/2A charger, but no power adapter is included. On a 1A source, five or more AA cells drop to 250mA each.
- It comes with a 12-month warranty and 30-day returns, and you pay return shipping.
- [Buy the Tenergy TN480U](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger). This is an affiliate link, and the price was verified on 2026-10-21.

## Tips
- Make sure the charger has independent slots so one weak cell doesn't hold up the others.
- With 16 cells, a full load takes longer and draws more power.
- None of these charge alkaline or lithium cells.

If you tell me your budget and how many cells you usually charge, I can narrow it down.
